title: Latency safeguard orchestration with backpressure matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a regional routing orchestration layer that enforces latency SLOs by combining real-time latency signals, per-region capacity headroom, and a configurable backpressure matrix. The goal is to enable graceful request evacuation, capacity-aware shedding, and automated circuit protection without disrupting affinity-critical traffic. This ticket covers policy definition, runtime integration, canary rollout, and observability changes.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine evaluates per-request region score using latency SLO delta + capacity headroom and returns routing decision within 5ms median
Under synthetic overload (30% above provisioned qps) steady-state p95 latency degradation limited to <15% for pinned customers, with non-pinned requests shed according to configured budget
Circuit breaker transitions (open/half-open/closed) respected; automatic fallback to compatible model variant or region within 2s
Canary rollout completed (10% traffic) with no customer-facing errors and metrics meeting SLO thresholds for 24h
Dashboards and alerts: per-region SLO burn rate, backpressure matrix heatmap, and a synthetic-traffic playbook exist and are linked
comments: 2025-01-28 - Triage: High-level design reviewed with SRE/Serving. Agreed to keep affinity rules (geo-pinning) as strong hints rather than absolute pins to enable graceful shedding in extreme load.
2025-01-30 - Design note: Chose continuous scoring model (latency delta normalized + capacity factor) instead of hard thresholds to avoid oscillation during transient spikes.
2025-02-03 - Proto: Lightweight policy service implemented (routing-score v0) and integrated into request director in canary cluster. Observed median decision time ~3.2ms in canary; acceptable.

2025-02-05 - Trade-off: To minimize blast radius we will not perform global automatic evacuation; fallback will be tiered: local region -> regional sibling -> cross-region failover. Will document expected increased tail latency for cross-region fallback.

2025-02-08 - Load test: Injected 40% traffic surge to us-west-2; backpressure matrix correctly ramped to shed non-pinned low-priority traffic and tripped circuit-breaker for overloaded worker pool. No SLO breach for pinned enterprise tenants in canary.
2025-02-10 - PR opened for policy + director integration: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-routing/pull/612
2025-02-11 - Requested reviews: @maria-li (SRE), @kevin-cho (Serving runtime) — waiting on feedback about KV cache interaction during failover.
2025-02-12 - Note: Need to update runbooks and alert thresholds if we change default budge/shred ratios. Ops suggested a conservative initial shedding budget of 10% of non-pinned qps per-region.
notes: Monitoring: Add burn-rate alert to trigger early rollback and inform SRE runbook
Rollout plan: 1) internal test -> 2) 1% traffic canary -> 3) 10% traffic canary for 24h -> 4) ramp to 50% -> full rollout
Risks: Cross-region failover increases egress costs and can impact downstream auth services due to geo-sensitive tokens; will validate during canary
Next steps: Address KV cache invalidation during failover (blocking feedback from Kevin), finalize shedding budgets with support/product
